title: v-model on Components
description: Create custom components that support v-model for two‑way data binding.

slides.title: How v-model Works on Components
slides.content:
# The Magic Behind `v-model`

On a native input, `v-model` is syntax sugar for:
```html
<input :value="data" @input="data = $event.target.value">
```

On a custom component, it becomes:
```html
<CustomComponent :modelValue="data" @update:modelValue="data = $event" />
```

So your component must:
- Accept a `modelValue` prop.
- Emit an `update:modelValue` event with the new value.

slides.title: Multiple v-model Bindings (Vue 3)
slides.content:
# Binding Multiple Values

Vue 3 allows multiple `v-model` bindings by specifying an argument:

```html
<ChildComponent v-model:first-name="firstName" v-model:last-name="lastName" />
```

Inside the component, you accept props `firstName` and `lastName`, and emit `update:firstName` and `update:lastName`.

```javascript
// Child component
export default {
  props: ['firstName', 'lastName'],
  emits: ['update:firstName', 'update:lastName']
}
```

quizData.question: To make a custom component work with `v-model`, what must the component do?

options.text: Accept a `value` prop and emit an `input` event
Accept a `modelValue` prop and emit an `update:modelValue` event
Use the `v-model` directive inside its template

quizData.explanation: In Vue 3, the default convention for `v-model` on components is to bind to `modelValue` prop and listen for `update:modelValue` event.
